plain: Not able to be divided or separated.

webster.text: That cannot be divided, separated or broken; not separable into parts.

example.quote: are aimed at each other, or at one indivisible object.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, June 27, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
